#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-3] stage_timeout_s precedence: template value beats
# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats the 5400 s engine default, each tier
# verified in isolation.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where stage_timeout_s is not a
# recognized template field and _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* is never exported)
# and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-3] stage_timeout_s precedence: template > env > 5400 s default"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-precedence"

_MINIMAL_HEAD='id: t
name: T
extends: null
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
'

_write_tpl() {
    printf '%s%s' "$_MINIMAL_HEAD" "$2" > "$1"
}

# ─── Tier 1: template value beats ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S ─────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] template stage_timeout_s beats ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S"

_tpl_t1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/t1.yaml"
_write_tpl "$_tpl_t1" 'flow:
  - alpha

alpha:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 7200
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=99 load_template "$_tpl_t1" >/dev/null 2>&1
_got="${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_alpha:-<unset>}"
assert_eq "[#1801/SPEC-3] template stage_timeout_s=7200 beats env ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=99" \
    "7200" "$_got"

# ─── Tier 2: ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats the 5400 s default ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats 5400 s engine default"

_tpl_t2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/t2.yaml"
_write_tpl "$_tpl_t2" 'flow:
  - beta

beta:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'
# No stage_timeout_s in template; env variable should win over 5400 default.
ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=1800 load_template "$_tpl_t2" >/dev/null 2>&1

# After the change: when the template doesn't declare stage_timeout_s,
# the engine resolves it at dispatch time from ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S > 5400.
# The template loader may not embed the env-tier value; the lookup contract
# is that ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S is consulted at dispatch.
# Assert that the template does NOT override with 5400 when ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S is set:
# the loaded var is either absent (resolved at dispatch) or equals the env value.
_got_t2="${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_beta:-<unset>}"
if [[ "$_got_t2" == "<unset>" || "$_got_t2" == "1800" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] template without stage_timeout_s does not hard-code 5400 (env tier respected)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] template without stage_timeout_s does not hard-code 5400 (env tier respected)" \
        "got _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_beta=${_got_t2} — must be unset or 1800 when ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=1800"
fi
unset ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S

# Verify the dispatch path (plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh) consults
# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S as tier-2: its body must reference it.
_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
_phc_body_t2=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body_t2="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S' <<< "$_phc_body_t2"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] dispatch consults ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S as tier-2 fallback (plugin_hook_call)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] dispatch consults ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S as tier-2 fallback (plugin_hook_call)" \
        "ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S not found in plugin_hook_call — env tier is not applied at dispatch"
fi

# ─── Tier 3: engine default is 5400 when neither template nor env sets it ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] engine default is 5400 s when neither template nor env sets stage_timeout_s"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
_runner_sh="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# Verify 5400 appears as the terminal fallback inside plugin_hook_call, not just
# anywhere in the file — a constant in a comment or unrelated context would pass
# the old grep but would not prove the default is actually applied at dispatch.
_phc_body_t3=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body_t3="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

if grep -qE '_lc_hook_to=5400|ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-5400' <<< "$_phc_body_t3"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] 5400 s is the terminal fallback in plugin_hook_call (tier-3 default)"
else
    # Also accept the default in runner.sh's always_run path for defence-in-depth.
    _has_5400_source=0
    if grep -qE '\b5400\b' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
        _has_5400_source=1
    fi
    if grep -qE '\b5400\b' "$_runner_sh" 2>/dev/null; then
        _has_5400_source=1
    fi
    if [[ "$_has_5400_source" -eq 1 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] 5400 s default appears as the engine's stage_timeout_s fallback"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] 5400 s default appears as the engine's stage_timeout_s fallback" \
            "5400 not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — the engine default is missing"
    fi
fi

# ─── Template parse: stage_timeout_s is exported as _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* ────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] load_template exports _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>"

_tpl_t3="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/t3.yaml"
_write_tpl "$_tpl_t3" 'flow:
  - gamma

gamma:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 3600
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

unset _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_gamma 2>/dev/null || true
load_template "$_tpl_t3" >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "[#1801/SPEC-3] load_template sets _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_gamma from stage_timeout_s" \
    "3600" "${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_gamma:-<unset>}"

# ─── Tier 3 isolation: actually RUNS dispatch with no template and no env var ──
# The requirement calls for "an isolation test that runs with neither a template
# value nor ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S set and confirms 5400 s is the timeout
# actually used." This section runs plugin_hook_call in a clean subprocess
# with a fake `sleep` binary that logs its first argument, then checks the
# log for exactly "5400". On pre-change code (no watchdog in plugin_hook_call)
# no sleep is spawned and the log is empty → FAIL. On post-change code the
# watchdog fires `sleep 5400` → the log contains "5400" → PASS.
#
# Timing: the watchdog and hook both start concurrently.  If zbuild_run()
# exits immediately, wait() returns before the watchdog gets to run sleep 5400,
# and the watchdog is killed before it can log its argument.  To avoid this
# race a FIFO rendezvous is used: the fake sleep logs "5400" and then writes
# one byte to the FIFO; zbuild_run() blocks reading the FIFO.  This guarantees
# "5400" is in the log before the hook exits and before the watchdog is killed.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] isolation: 5400 s default confirmed by running plugin_hook_call"

_spec3_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-fakebin"
_spec3_log="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-sleep-log.txt"
_spec3_fifo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-rendezvous"
rm -f "$_spec3_log" "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$_spec3_bin"
mkfifo "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true

# Fake sleep: logs its first arg; when arg is 5400 (watchdog timer) also
# signals the hook via the FIFO so the hook can exit.  The log write is
# unconditional and happens BEFORE the FIFO write — "5400" is therefore
# always in the log even if the FIFO signal races with watchdog cleanup.
cat > "$_spec3_bin/sleep" <<FAKESLEEP
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "\$1" >> "$_spec3_log"
[[ "\$1" == "5400" ]] && printf 'go' > "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0
FAKESLEEP
chmod +x "$_spec3_bin/sleep"

# Mock plugin: zbuild_run blocks on the FIFO rendezvous (3 s safety timeout).
# Without this wait the hook exits before the watchdog starts sleep 5400 and
# the watchdog is killed before it can log its argument — the race this FIFO
# eliminates.
_spec3_plugin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-plugin"
mkdir -p "$_spec3_plugin"
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # $TEST_TEMP_DIR expands here, not inside the heredoc
cat > "$_spec3_plugin/plugin.sh" <<PLUGIN
zbuild_run() {
    # Wait for the watchdog to signal via FIFO (or give up after 3 s).
    read -r -t 3 _sig < "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
}
PLUGIN
cat > "$_spec3_plugin/manifest.yaml" <<'MANIFEST'
id: spec3-isolation
name: Spec3 Isolation Mock
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: zbuild_run
MANIFEST
_spec3_state="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-state.json"
printf '{"pipeline_status":"running"}' > "$_spec3_state"

# Run plugin_hook_call in a clean subshell:
# - PATH prepended with our fake sleep
# - ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S unset (no tier-2 value)
# - No _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_spec3isolation (no tier-1 value)
# The watchdog should resolve to the 5400 s tier-3 default.
(
    export PATH="$_spec3_bin:$PATH"
    unset ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S
    unset _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_spec3isolation
    export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE=spec3isolation
    # Source the full registry facade so yaml_get (manifest-validation.sh) and
    # verify_plugin_for_source (discovery.sh) are defined before lifecycle.sh
    # calls them — lifecycle.sh declares it "depends on yaml_get /
    # verify_plugin_for_source from the other two split modules — sourced together
    # via the registry.sh facade" and must not be sourced in isolation.
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
    plugin_hook_call "$_spec3_plugin" run spec3isolation "$_spec3_state" 2>/dev/null || true
) 2>/dev/null || true

_spec3_found_5400=0
if [[ -f "$_spec3_log" ]] && grep -qE '^5400$' "$_spec3_log"; then
    _spec3_found_5400=1
fi

if [[ "$_spec3_found_5400" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] isolation: plugin_hook_call spawns 'sleep 5400' watchdog when no template value and no ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] isolation: plugin_hook_call spawns 'sleep 5400' watchdog when no template value and no ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S" \
        "no 'sleep 5400' captured in fake-sleep log — pre-change: no watchdog; post-change: must spawn 'sleep 5400' as default"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Guard: enumerate every engine path that still returns an rc outside {0,1}
     3	# (#1823, ADR-054 §4) — and make the list a RATCHET.
     4	#
     5	# ADR-054 §4 gives #1823 "the narrowing and the designs that re-home each
     6	# signal", with the enforcing check being "no engine path returns or interprets
     7	# an rc outside {0,1}, with a guard test enumerating the call sites". That plain
     8	# assertion cannot hold yet and saying otherwise would be a lie: the legacy
     9	# vocabulary is still in flight during versioned coexistence, and #1850 deletes
    10	# it together with the v1 result reader ("the legacy rc mapping (5, 8, 9, 10,
    11	# 11) is deleted; a guard asserts no engine path returns an rc outside {0,1}").
    12	#
    13	# So this guard enumerates instead of forbidding, and ratchets:
    14	#
    15	#   * a count that RISES fails    — a new engine path grew a private rc
    16	#   * a count that FALLS fails    — progress must be locked in, not left
    17	#                                   as slack for the next one to spend
    18	#
    19	# #1850 emptied these: the pin is zero across the board and §SPEC-16 below
    20	# states the plain rule its acceptance describes. The ratchet stays so a raise
    21	# names the file that grew.
    22	#
    23	# Counting `return N` / `exit N` textually is deliberately crude. It cannot be
    24	# fooled in the direction that matters — adding a new private rc adds a line —
    25	# and a guard that parsed control flow would be a second implementation of the
    26	# thing under test.
    27	#
    28	# KNOWN BLIND SPOT, verified by running this file against the merge-base: an rc
    29	# behind a named constant (`return "$ZBUILD_HOOK_ABSENT"`) is invisible to a
    30	# literal count, so §1's numbers would have read as clean while ADR-056's rc=3
    31	# was live. Widening the pattern to `return "$VAR"` is not the answer — it would
    32	# flag every legitimate `return $rc` passthrough, of which the engine has many.
    33	# Named sentinels are therefore asserted BY NAME in §2 as they are found. If a
    34	# future one appears, it needs its own named assertion; the count will not catch
    35	# it. Recorded rather than papered over: a guard whose limits are undocumented
    36	# is trusted for more than it checks.
    37	set -euo pipefail
    38	
    39	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    40	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    41	
    42	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
    43	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
    44	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
    45	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
    46	
    47	print_test_header "dispatch-rc guard — the legacy rc inventory is a ratchet (#1823)"
    48	
    49	# The repo default `grep` may be ugrep; use the system one for stable -cE.
    50	SYSGREP=/usr/bin/grep
    51	
    52	# #1850 added the strategies' shared helpers, stage-scratch, disposition, the
    53	# contract validator and the orch backends' collect, all now 0.
    54	# The engine files ADR-054 §4 names. Scoped deliberately: scripts/lib/worktree.sh,
    55	# scripts/lib/git-remote.sh, core/output/stage-io.sh and friends have their own
    56	# unrelated private rc vocabularies that collide numerically but are not the
    57	# engine↔stage contract. Widening this list to "every .sh" would bury the
    58	# signal under ~40 unrelated call sites.
    59	#
    60	# THE PIN. Each number is "legacy rc returns in this file today". Lower it when
    61	# you remove one; you may never raise it.
    62	#
    63	# #2111 raised runner.sh 35→36 and cycle-orchestrator.sh 29→30: NOT a new word —
    64	# rc=9 is the llm-abort channel #1024 declared and _zbuild_propagate_abort has
    65	# carried since then. These two are the enforcing callers it never had (the
    66	# disposition table's `halt_unavailable` was announced, not acted on), and the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh — when a stage's latest run started, and
# whether a result was written by it (ADR-068 §8).
#
# The engine never deletes a stage's output. So a stage that runs again and
# writes nothing leaves its previous result in place, and every reader must not
# take that result as this run's. One writer and one check, so no reader can
# decide it differently: _verdict_read_result, the stage report, build_kind and
# gate-aggregator all ask stage_result_is_current.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_DISPATCH_MARK_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_DISPATCH_MARK_LOADED=1

# stage_dispatch_mark_path <state_dir> <stage>
stage_dispatch_mark_path() {
    printf '%s/runtime/dispatched/%s' "$1" "${2//[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/_}"
}

# stage_dispatch_mark <state_file> <stage> — record that <stage> starts a run
# now. Fail-open: a stage is never refused over bookkeeping.
stage_dispatch_mark() {
    local state_file="${1:-}" stage="${2:-}" m
    [[ "$state_file" == /* && -n "$stage" ]] || return 0
    m="$(stage_dispatch_mark_path "$(dirname "$state_file")" "$stage")"
    mkdir -p "${m%/*}" 2>/dev/null && : > "$m" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# stage_result_is_current <state_dir> <stage> <result_file> — rc 1 when the
# result is older than <stage>'s latest run, i.e. that run wrote none. No mark
# means the stage has not run in this state dir: its result is its latest
# output, whichever run wrote it (ADR-068 §8).
stage_result_is_current() {
    local m
    [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || return 0
    m="$(stage_dispatch_mark_path "$1" "$2")"
    [[ -e "$m" && "$m" -nt "$3" ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

# ─── verify_plugin_for_source — pre-source tamper check (#290) ──────────────
# Returns 0 if plugin.sh is safe to source per the lockfile, 1 if tampered.
# When ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK=1, this is called from plugin_hook_call right
# before `source "$plugin_sh"`; mismatch refuses to source. When the env var
# is unset (default), behavior matches lockfile_validate: warn-only.
#
# If no lockfile entry exists for this plugin, returns 0 — the lockfile is
# the authority on what's pinned, and a brand-new plugin won't be there yet.
verify_plugin_for_source() {
    local manifest="$1"
    local lockfile="${2:-$ZBUILD_LOCKFILE}"
    [[ ! -f "$lockfile" ]] && return 0

    local id; id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id")"
    [[ -z "$id" ]] && return 0

    local expected_pair manifest_in_lock
    while IFS=' ' read -r lock_id pair lock_manifest; do
        if [[ "$lock_id" == "$id" ]]; then
            expected_pair="$pair"
            manifest_in_lock="$lock_manifest"
            break
        fi
    done < "$lockfile"

    # No entry — new plugin, no pin to enforce.
    [[ -z "${expected_pair:-}" ]] && return 0

    # Legacy single-hash record: insist on regeneration before enforcing.
    if [[ "$expected_pair" != *:* ]]; then
        warn "verify_plugin_for_source: $id has legacy single-hash lockfile entry; cannot verify plugin.sh (#290)"
        [[ "${ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 1
        return 0
    fi

    local actual_pair; actual_pair="$(_hash_plugin_pair "$manifest")"
    if [[ "$actual_pair" != "$expected_pair" ]]; then
        # kind carried for the envelope (#1705): the tamper check runs during
        # discovery, outside plugin_hook_call's exported context. `:-unknown`
        # matches contracts.sh — a manifest that fails to parse is exactly the
        # case this check fires on, and an empty kind would leave the envelope
        # blank for the one event most worth attributing.
        local _kind; _kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        emit_event "plugin.tamper.detected" "plugin=$id" \
            "kind=${_kind:-unknown}" \
            "manifest=$manifest_in_lock"
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
            error "verify_plugin_for_source: $id — file hash mismatch (lockfile: $expected_pair, actual: $actual_pair). plugin.sh or manifest.yaml has changed since lock; refusing to source under ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK=1."
            return 1
        fi
        warn "verify_plugin_for_source: $id — file hash mismatch (lockfile: $expected_pair, actual: $actual_pair). plugin.sh or manifest.yaml has changed since lock. Set ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK=1 to refuse to source on mismatch."
        return 0
    fi
    return 0
}

# ─── find_plugin_for_role ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Find a plugin directory providing the given role and backend alias.
# Usage: find_plugin_for_role <role> <backend_alias> [plugins_root]
# Output: prints plugin_dir on success; returns 1 if not found.
# Matches by: provides.role == <role> AND (id == <alias> OR provides.alias == <alias>)
find_plugin_for_role() {
    local role="$1"

print_test_results() {
    if [[ "${SKIP:-0}" -gt 0 ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}${BOLD}SKIP${RESET}"
        echo ""
        # #1063 follow-up: record this file as skipped so run-tests.sh can report
        # skips distinctly. A skipped file exits 0 and would otherwise tally as a
        # PASS, hiding platform gating (e.g. #996's skip_on_platform macos shows up
        # as a confusing "172/172 passed" with no indication 8 tests were skipped).
        [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_SKIP_LOG:-}" ]] \
            && printf '%s\n' "${0##*/}" >> "$ZBUILD_TEST_SKIP_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
        exit 0
    fi
    # #600: in quiet mode, emit a single-line compact summary FIRST so the
    # pipeline operator can scan a 30-line test-stage banner instead of ~150.
    # The full multi-line block follows unchanged (no info loss for humans
    # reviewing failures).
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        if [[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo -e "  ${GREEN}${BOLD}✓ ${PASS}/${TOTAL} passed${RESET}"
        else
            echo -e "  ${RED}${BOLD}✗ ${PASS}/${TOTAL} passed (${FAIL} FAILED)${RESET}"
        fi
    fi
    echo ""
    echo -e "${DIM}  ──────────────────────────────────────────${RESET}"
    echo ""
    if [[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}${BOLD}All $TOTAL tests passed${RESET}"
    else
        echo -e "  ${RED}${BOLD}$FAIL of $TOTAL tests failed${RESET}"
        echo ""
        for f in "${FAILURES[@]}"; do
            echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} $f"
        done
    fi
    echo ""
    exit "$FAIL"
}

# Mock route_to_model with parameterizable rc, stdout, and optional delay
# Usage: mock_route_to_model <rc> <stdout_content> [delay_seconds]
mock_route_to_model() {
  local rc="$1"
  local stdout_content="$2"
  local delay="${3:-0}"
  local mock_dir="${ZBUILD_TEST_TMP:-/tmp}/mocks/$$"
  mkdir -p "$mock_dir"
  # Write stdout content to a file so single-quotes in content don't break the script
  printf '%s' "$stdout_content" > "$mock_dir/claude-stdout"

# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do

    fi
done

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] specific named routes: cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf ──
# runner.sh hosts three explicit dispatch routes that all must reach plugin_hook_call:
#   cycle_dispatch_stage      — cycle member (calls plugin_hook_call for each member/iteration)
#   parallel_dispatch_stage   — parallel-group member (concurrent per-member dispatch)
#   roleless leaf             — direct dispatch when the template has no roles (backward compat)
# Each is explicitly verified below so a refactor that moves one of them out of lifecycle.sh
# without updating the watchdog would cause these assertions to fail.

_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# cycle member — extract function body (4-space indented in runner.sh)
_cycle_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _cycle_fn_body="$(awk '/^    cycle_dispatch_stage\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{p=0;exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_cycle_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] cycle member: cycle_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] cycle member: cycle_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call" \
        "plugin_hook_call not found inside cycle_dispatch_stage — cycle members bypass the per-dispatch watchdog"
fi

# parallel-group member — extract function body
_parallel_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _parallel_fn_body="$(awk '/^    parallel_dispatch_stage\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{p=0;exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_parallel_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] parallel-group member: parallel_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"

fi

# always_run route — AWK-extract _runner_dispatch_always_run body and confirm it calls plugin_hook_call.
# SPEC-1 requires this to be established via body extraction, not a file-level grep on runner.sh,
# so that a refactor moving the dispatch call out of the function cannot slip through.
_always_run_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _always_run_fn_body="$(awk '/_runner_dispatch_always_run\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_always_run_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] always_run route: _runner_dispatch_always_run in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"

# runner.sh has MULTIPLE occurrences of `[[ -z "$roles_out" ]]`: the first is a dry-run

    _roleless_found="$(awk '
        /\[\[ -z "\$roles_out" \]\]/ { block=40 }
        block > 0 {
            if (/plugin_hook_call/) { found=1; exit }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads stage_timeout_s (not
# router.timeout_s) for its time limit; simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s
# for all stages at required values; router.timeout_s remains absent from the
# two always_run stages.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run kills through zbuild_pg_kill;
# no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for stage dispatch.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where _runner_dispatch_always_run reads
# _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* and uses a hand-rolled kill sequence) and PASS
# after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-6] always_run uses stage_timeout_s; [#1801/SPEC-10] zbuild_pg_kill"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-always-run"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] runner.sh reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _ROUTER_TIMEOUT ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"

_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# Extract the _runner_dispatch_always_run function body.
_ar_body=""
_ar_body="$(awk '/_runner_dispatch_always_run\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"

if [[ -z "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh" \
        "function body not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run is defined in runner.sh"

    # After the change: reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*, not _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*
    if grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run reads _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*" \
            "_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* not found — still using old _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* or ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT"
    fi

    # The OLD variable must not be the primary source.
    # It may still exist as a fallback to ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S, but
    # _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* must NOT be the limit variable the function uses.
    if grep -q '_ar_to.*_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT\|_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT.*_ar_to' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit" \
            "still reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* for _ar_to — must use _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* instead"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] _runner_dispatch_always_run no longer uses _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_* as its time limit"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml carries stage_timeout_s for all stages ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml stage_timeout_s values"

_simple="$REPO_ROOT/config/templates/simple.yaml"
if [[ ! -f "$_simple" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] config/templates/simple.yaml exists" "not found"
else
    # ── [#1801/SPEC-6] REQUIRED VALUES: release=30, persist=120 ──────────────
    # Direct assertions for the two values SPEC-6 explicitly mandates.
    # Not inside a helper function so the requirement is unambiguously visible.
    _spec6_r="$(awk '/^release:/{f=1; next} f && /^[a-zA-Z_-]/{exit} f && /stage_timeout_s:/{print; exit}' \
        "$_simple" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)"
    if [[ "$_spec6_r" == "30" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml release: stage_timeout_s == 30 (required)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml release: stage_timeout_s == 30 (required)" \
            "got '${_spec6_r:-<absent>}' — SPEC-6 mandates stage_timeout_s 30 for release"
    fi

    _spec6_p="$(awk '/^persist:/{f=1; next} f && /^[a-zA-Z_-]/{exit} f && /stage_timeout_s:/{print; exit}' \
        "$_simple" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)"
    if [[ "$_spec6_p" == "120" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml persist: stage_timeout_s == 120 (required)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml persist: stage_timeout_s == 120 (required)" \
            "got '${_spec6_p:-<absent>}' — SPEC-6 mandates stage_timeout_s 120 for persist"
    fi

    # Verify required stage_timeout_s values by parsing the template.
    # Each check verifies that the section contains `stage_timeout_s: N`.
    # Strategy: for each stage, confirm that stage_timeout_s appears in simple.yaml
    # with the required value by extracting the section and checking.
    _check_stage_timeout() {
        local _stage="$1" _expected_s="$2"
        # Find the stage section and look for stage_timeout_s: N within it.
        # Use awk to extract from the stage heading to the next top-level entry.
        local _found
        _found="$(awk -v stage="$_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /stage_timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+')"

        if [[ "$_found" == "$_expected_s" ]]; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_stage: stage_timeout_s == ${_expected_s}s" \
                "got '${_found:-<absent>}'"
        fi
    }

    _check_stage_timeout "release" "30"
    _check_stage_timeout "persist" "120"
    _check_stage_timeout "test" "5400"
    _check_stage_timeout "build" "4200"
    _check_stage_timeout "design" "3900"
    _check_stage_timeout "plan" "1200"
    _check_stage_timeout "test-author" "900"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-coverage" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "acceptance-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "issue-acceptance" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "spec-correspondence" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review_lenses" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "intake" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "pr" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "hydrate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "secret-scan" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "shape-floor" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "design-gate" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "gate-aggregator" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "assertion-integrity" "600"
    _check_stage_timeout "review-aggregator" "600"

    # ─── [#1801/SPEC-6] release and persist have no router.timeout_s ──────────
    # The two always_run stages convert their router.timeout_s to stage_timeout_s.
    # After the change they must not declare router.timeout_s.
    for _ar_stage in release persist; do
        _router_to=""
        _router_to="$(awk -v stage="$_ar_stage:" '
            $0 == stage { in_stage=1; next }
            in_stage && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { exit }
            in_stage && /router:/ { in_router=1; next }
            in_stage && in_router && /timeout_s:/ { print; exit }
            in_stage && in_router && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z_]+:/ && !/timeout_s/ { in_router=0 }
        ' "$_simple" 2>/dev/null || true)"

        if [[ -n "$_router_to" ]]; then
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)" \
                "router.timeout_s still present: $_router_to"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-6] simple.yaml $_ar_stage: no router.timeout_s (converted to stage_timeout_s)"
        fi
    done
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run uses zbuild_pg_kill"

if [[ -n "$_ar_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run calls zbuild_pg_kill" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found in function body"
    fi

    # The hand-rolled `kill -(TERM|KILL) -- -"$_ar_pid"` pattern must be gone from
    # this function — it bypasses zbuild_pg_kill's TERM+grace+KILL sequence.
    if grep -qE 'kill -(TERM|KILL) -- -"\$_ar_pid"' <<< "$_ar_body"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence" \
            "found 'kill -TERM/-KILL -- -\"\$_ar_pid\"' — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch ──────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill (not hand-rolled TERM/KILL) for dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' "$_lc"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh calls zbuild_pg_kill for stage dispatch" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — the per-dispatch watchdog must use it"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-2] Killing a hung run hook stops the entire process group — a
# child ignoring TERM leaves no process alive after TERM + 10 s grace.
#
# The per-dispatch watchdog must:
#   1. Run the hook subshell under set -m (job-control mode) so the subshell
#      becomes a process-group leader.
#   2. Kill via zbuild_pg_kill, which sends TERM to the whole group and then
#      KILL after a grace period.
#   3. The grace period must be at least 10 s (so a hook that traps TERM has
#      enough time to flush, but a child ignoring TERM is killed).
#
# These tests use source-level checks — the behavioral guarantee (no process
# survives) is enforced by SPEC-6b in the integration test. These FAIL on
# pre-change code (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog at all) and PASS after.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-2] hung run hook kills entire process group (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL)"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call arms the hook under set -m ──────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call runs the hook under set -m (creates a process group)"

_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    # set -m inside the function creates a new process group for the backgrounded subshell
    if grep -q 'set -m' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses set -m to give the hook its own process group" \
            "'set -m' not found in plugin_hook_call — the hook's group cannot be signalled"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the kill goes through zbuild_pg_kill (group-scope) ────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the timeout kill uses zbuild_pg_kill (group scope, not single-PID)"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] plugin_hook_call uses zbuild_pg_kill (sends signal to whole group)" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill not found — a single-PID kill cannot reach descendants that ignore TERM"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM + grace + KILL ──────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM then KILL after grace (proc-group.sh)"

_pg="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_pg" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] scripts/lib/proc-group.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # zbuild_pg_kill must delegate to _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill, which does
    # TERM → poll → KILL.
    if grep -q '_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill' "$_pg"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] zbuild_pg_kill uses TERM+grace+KILL sequence (_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill)" \
            "_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill not found in proc-group.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] the grace is at least 10 s ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] the watchdog grace period is at least 10 s"

# The design specifies TERM + 10 s grace + KILL. Verify that the watchdog in
# lifecycle.sh passes a grace of >= 10 to zbuild_pg_kill or that the default
# grace in _zbuild_pg_grace is sufficiently large.
# Check that the value 10 (or larger) appears in the context of zbuild_pg_kill
# invocations in lifecycle.sh.
if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # Look for zbuild_pg_kill called with a numeric grace >= 10.
    # Accept the pattern: zbuild_pg_kill "$var" 10 or zbuild_pg_kill "$pid" "$grace"
    # where the literal in the source is >= 10.
    _grace_ok=0
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill.*[[:space:]][0-9]+' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        # Extract all numeric values following zbuild_pg_kill
        while IFS= read -r _val; do
            [[ "$_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_val" -ge 10 ]] && { _grace_ok=1; break; }
        done < <(grep -oE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
    fi
    # Also accept if the grace is passed via a variable (the design uses a configurable grace)
    if grep -qE 'zbuild_pg_kill[^)]*\$\{?[A-Za-z_]' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        _grace_ok=1
    fi

    if [[ "$_grace_ok" -eq 1 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] watchdog grace period is >= 10 s (or variable-derived)" \
            "no zbuild_pg_kill call with grace >= 10 found in plugin_hook_call"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap is in the run-hook branch, not at function scope ─
# SPEC-2: "plugin_hook_call's run-hook branch has a TERM trap ... that kills the
# inner hook group and watchdog and exits with status 143 when plugin_hook_call is
# externally TERMed, so the hook's children are not orphaned"
# A trap at function scope would catch TERM for ALL hook types (cleanup, etc.)
# which is wrong; the trap must be confined to the run-hook branch only.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap is inside the run-hook branch (not at function scope)"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # Extract ONLY the run-hook branch: from `if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then`
    # to the matching `    else` at 4-space indent. The trap must be in THIS block,
    # not at function scope where it would fire for cleanup hooks too.
    _run_branch=""
    _run_branch="$(awk '
        /if \[\[ "\$hook_name" == "run" \]\]; then/{in_run=1}
        in_run{print}
        in_run && /^    else/{exit}
    ' <<< "$_phc_body" 2>/dev/null || true)"

    if [[ -z "$_run_branch" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] run-hook branch is identifiable in plugin_hook_call" \
            "could not extract 'if hook_name == run' block — guard not found or awk pattern mismatch"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] run-hook branch is identifiable in plugin_hook_call"

        # The TERM trap must be inside the run-hook branch — old code had no trap at all.
        if grep -q 'trap.*TERM' <<< "$_run_branch"; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap is inside the run-hook branch (not at function scope)"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap is inside the run-hook branch (not at function scope)" \
                "no 'trap ... TERM' found in run-hook branch — a function-scope trap would affect cleanup hooks"
        fi

        # The TERM trap must exit with status 143 (128 + SIGTERM=15).
        if grep -q 'exit 143' <<< "$_run_branch"; then
            assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap in run-hook branch exits with status 143"
        else
            assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] TERM trap in run-hook branch exits with status 143" \
                "'exit 143' not found in run-hook branch — the TERM trap must exit 143 (128+SIGTERM)"
        fi
    fi
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
# stage dispatch.
#
# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

    # The watchdog must be armed only for the `run` hook (not cleanup/other hooks).
    # Check for a guard like `[[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]` near the timeout code.
    if grep -qE '"run"' <<< "$_phc_body" && grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"

# The watchdog fires when rc=143 (SIGTERM from zbuild_pg_kill) or rc=137
# (SIGKILL).  lifecycle.sh handles this with:
#
#   if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
#       emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=..." "kind=..." \
#           "stage=..." "timeout_s=..." "disposition=timed_out"
#   fi
#
# The emit_event call IS the result-contract write for the timed_out
# disposition (ADR-054 §9): it records disposition=timed_out, the stage
# name, and the limit in the event stream.  Verify directly that the
# plugin.run.timed_out emit_event in lifecycle.sh carries disposition=timed_out.
_timed_out_event_ctx=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _timed_out_event_ctx="$(grep -A5 'plugin\.run\.timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
fi

# Direct verification: disposition=timed_out is in the emit_event block.
if grep -q 'disposition=timed_out' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition=timed_out in the plugin.run.timed_out emit_event call (result-contract write)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition=timed_out in the plugin.run.timed_out emit_event call (result-contract write)" \
        "disposition=timed_out not found in the 5 lines after 'plugin.run.timed_out' in lifecycle.sh — the disposition is not written on timeout"
fi

# The timed_out event must also name the stage and the limit.
if grep -q 'stage=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx" && grep -q 'timeout_s=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)" \
        "plugin.run.timed_out event in lifecycle.sh is missing stage= or timeout_s= field"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"

# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls

for _sf in \

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] specific named routes: cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf ──

_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# cycle member — extract function body (4-space indented in runner.sh)
_cycle_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then

fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_cycle_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] cycle member: cycle_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] cycle member: cycle_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call" \
        "plugin_hook_call not found inside cycle_dispatch_stage — cycle members bypass the per-dispatch watchdog"
fi

# parallel-group member — extract function body
_parallel_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _parallel_fn_body="$(awk '/^    parallel_dispatch_stage\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{p=0;exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_parallel_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] parallel-group member: parallel_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] parallel-group member: parallel_dispatch_stage in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call" \
        "plugin_hook_call not found inside parallel_dispatch_stage — parallel members bypass the per-dispatch watchdog"
fi

# always_run route — AWK-extract _runner_dispatch_always_run body and confirm it calls plugin_hook_call.
# SPEC-1 requires this to be established via body extraction, not a file-level grep on runner.sh,
# so that a refactor moving the dispatch call out of the function cannot slip through.
_always_run_fn_body=""
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _always_run_fn_body="$(awk '/_runner_dispatch_always_run\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^    \}$/{exit}' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' <<< "$_always_run_fn_body"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] always_run route: _runner_dispatch_always_run in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] always_run route: _runner_dispatch_always_run in runner.sh calls plugin_hook_call" \
        "plugin_hook_call not found inside _runner_dispatch_always_run body — always_run stages bypass the per-dispatch watchdog"
fi

# roleless leaf — the path taken when the stage has no template roles (backward-compat direct dispatch)
# In runner.sh: if [[ -z "$roles_out" ]] … plugin_hook_call … else (strategy dispatch)
# runner.sh has MULTIPLE occurrences of `[[ -z "$roles_out" ]]`: the first is a dry-run

# We scan ALL occurrences, capturing up to 40 lines after each, and check whether ANY

_roleless_found=0
if [[ -f "$_runner" ]]; then
    _roleless_found="$(awk '

# ─── Tier 3 isolation: actually RUNS dispatch with no template and no env var ──
# The requirement calls for "an isolation test that runs with neither a template
# value nor ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S set and confirms 5400 s is the timeout
# actually used." This section runs plugin_hook_call in a clean subprocess
# with a fake `sleep` binary that logs its first argument, then checks the
# log for exactly "5400". On pre-change code (no watchdog in plugin_hook_call)
# no sleep is spawned and the log is empty → FAIL. On post-change code the
# watchdog fires `sleep 5400` → the log contains "5400" → PASS.
#
# Timing: the watchdog and hook both start concurrently.  If zbuild_run()
# exits immediately, wait() returns before the watchdog gets to run sleep 5400,
# and the watchdog is killed before it can log its argument.  To avoid this
# race a FIFO rendezvous is used: the fake sleep logs "5400" and then writes
# one byte to the FIFO; zbuild_run() blocks reading the FIFO.  This guarantees
# "5400" is in the log before the hook exits and before the watchdog is killed.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] isolation: 5400 s default confirmed by running plugin_hook_call"

_spec3_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-fakebin"
_spec3_log="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-sleep-log.txt"
_spec3_fifo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-rendezvous"
rm -f "$_spec3_log" "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$_spec3_bin"
mkfifo "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true

# Fake sleep: logs its first arg; when arg is 5400 (watchdog timer) also
# signals the hook via the FIFO so the hook can exit.  The log write is
# unconditional and happens BEFORE the FIFO write — "5400" is therefore
# always in the log even if the FIFO signal races with watchdog cleanup.
cat > "$_spec3_bin/sleep" <<FAKESLEEP
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "\$1" >> "$_spec3_log"
[[ "\$1" == "5400" ]] && printf 'go' > "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
exit 0
FAKESLEEP
chmod +x "$_spec3_bin/sleep"

# Mock plugin: zbuild_run blocks on the FIFO rendezvous (3 s safety timeout).
# Without this wait the hook exits before the watchdog starts sleep 5400 and
# the watchdog is killed before it can log its argument — the race this FIFO
# eliminates.
_spec3_plugin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec3-plugin"
mkdir -p "$_spec3_plugin"
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # $TEST_TEMP_DIR expands here, not inside the heredoc
cat > "$_spec3_plugin/plugin.sh" <<PLUGIN
zbuild_run() {
    # Wait for the watchdog to signal via FIFO (or give up after 3 s).
    read -r -t 3 _sig < "$_spec3_fifo" 2>/dev/null || true
}
PLUGIN

id: spec3-isolation
name: Spec3 Isolation Mock
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: zbuild_run
MANIFEST

printf '{"pipeline_status":"running"}' > "$_spec3_state"

# ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats the 5400 s engine default, each tier

# recognized template field and _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_* is never exported)
# and PASS after the change.

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-3] stage_timeout_s precedence: template > env > 5400 s default"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-precedence"

_MINIMAL_HEAD='id: t
name: T
extends: null
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
'

_write_tpl() {
    printf '%s%s' "$_MINIMAL_HEAD" "$2" > "$1"
}

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] template stage_timeout_s beats ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S"

_tpl_t1="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/t1.yaml"
_write_tpl "$_tpl_t1" 'flow:
  - alpha

alpha:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  stage_timeout_s: 7200
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=99 load_template "$_tpl_t1" >/dev/null 2>&1
_got="${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_alpha:-<unset>}"
assert_eq "[#1801/SPEC-3] template stage_timeout_s=7200 beats env ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=99" \
    "7200" "$_got"

# ─── Tier 2: ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats the 5400 s default ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S beats 5400 s engine default"

_tpl_t2="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/t2.yaml"
_write_tpl "$_tpl_t2" 'flow:
  - beta

beta:
  gate: auto
  roles: [intake]
  io:
    destinations: [file]
'

# the engine resolves it at dispatch time from ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S > 5400.
# The template loader may not embed the env-tier value; the lookup contract
# is that ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S is consulted at dispatch.

# the loaded var is either absent (resolved at dispatch) or equals the env value.
_got_t2="${_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_beta:-<unset>}"

    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] template without stage_timeout_s does not hard-code 5400 (env tier respected)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] template without stage_timeout_s does not hard-code 5400 (env tier respected)" \
        "got _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_beta=${_got_t2} — must be unset or 1800 when ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S=1800"

_phc_body_t2=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body_t2="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S' <<< "$_phc_body_t2"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-3] dispatch consults ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S as tier-2 fallback (plugin_hook_call)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-3] dispatch consults ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S as tier-2 fallback (plugin_hook_call)" \
        "ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S not found in plugin_hook_call — env tier is not applied at dispatch"
fi

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-3] engine default is 5400 s when neither template nor env sets stage_timeout_s"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"
_runner_sh="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
